blocks.html: On this subject I have sometimes seen it called into doubt, to see whether a man who is going to die can be heard as a witness, or otherwise examined by a Judge: seeing that in this kind of hearings memory and recollection are singularly required a, which cannot well fall to one who, feeling the last breaths of his life draw near, and overcome by the hideous fright and horrible apprehension of death, is agitated and tormented in a thousand and a thousand ways b.

notes.citation: Digest 47.2.32 (De furtis, l. Quidam tabular[um]), at the end
notes.original: l. quidam tabular. à la fin. D. de fur.

notes.citation: Code 6.23 (De testamentis), l. Hac consultissima (C. 6.23.21, Theodosius II and Valentinian III, 439), § At cum humana (paragraph number not verified)
notes.original: l. hac conſultiſſima. P. at cũ humana. C. de teſt.
notes.gloss: The paragraph on the frailty of the dying testator; cited again at {n}. The transcribers could not settle whether the print's double s is ſſ or ß; the word is the same.

blocks.html: In a thousand forms of death one single death wearies the wretched (Mille modis lethi miseros mors una fatigat) c.

notes.gloss: Mille modis leti miseros mors una fatigat — by a thousand kinds of death one death wearies the wretched.

blocks.html: Witness our Redeemer Jesus Christ, who, foretasting the sharpness and bitterness of his dolorous passion, was sorrowful at it even unto death d, nay even to the point of grieving, and almost complaining, of God his father, saying, Heli, Heli, lama sabathani? My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me e? Nevertheless the contrary opinion is, with great reason, practised and received by all. For if he who is at the extremity of life can dispose of his goods by testament, sale, gift, and any other kind of disposition whatsoever, whether between the living or by reason of death f (in which, however, the integrity of a man's sense and understanding is greatly required g) — nay even, says the Emperor, though the dying man, crushed by sickness, were half dead and stammered with his tongue, provided that otherwise his conceptions and wishes be understood h — why is it that for the same reasons (where the case shall require it) the dying man cannot be heard and bear witness i? True it is that in this I desire the Judge, or Commissioner, who proceeds to the hearing to be prudent, wise, discreet and well advised, not to make the interrogations confused, long or prolix, but the clearest and briefest he can, comprising in few words the whole substance of the business k; inasmuch as, as has been said above, the spirit of him who feels near at hand the tearing asunder and separation of body and soul (a thing which the pure philosophers have esteemed above all others horrible and frightful l, even to the wicked m), being infinitely travailed and afflicted, would be so still more if he found himself pressed to remember so many and so many things, about which he might be too curiously and prolixly searched n. For who is there (said Cicero) from whom, when death approaches, the blood does not withdraw, and who does not turn white with fright and fear?

notes.original: S. Matth. chap. xxvj. S. Marc c. xiiij.
notes.gloss: Tristis est anima mea usque ad mortem — my soul is sorrowful even unto death, at Gethsemane.
Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? The transcribers' first reading of the word is defective ([?]ſabathani); the alternative, aſabathani, is Coras's lama sabathani with the a carried to the second word.

notes.citation: Digest 32.39.1 (De legatis et fideicommissis III, l. Pamphilo, § Proposi[tum]); Bartolus (Bartole) on Digest 28.1 (Qui testamenta facere possunt), l. Heredes palam (D. 28.1.21, Ulpian), § Uno contextu (§ 3)
notes.original: l. Pamphylo P. propoſi. D. de leg. iij. Bar. l. hære. P. vno cont. D. de te.
notes.gloss: A testament must be made uno contextu, in one continuous act; Bartolus on the dying testator.

notes.citation: Digest 28.1 (Qui testamenta facere possunt), l. 2 (D. 28.1.2, Labeo)
notes.gloss: In eo qui testatur eius temporis, quo testamentum facit, integritas mentis, non corporis sanitas exigenda est — in a testator, soundness of mind, not health of body, is required at the time he makes the will. Coras's "integrity of a man's sense and understanding".

notes.original: l. quoniam indignum. C. de teſta.
notes.gloss: The emperor's law allowing the will of a testator who, though failing, can still make his wishes understood — Coras's "half dead and stammering".

notes.citation: Digest 28.1.26 (Qui testamenta facere possunt, l. Cum lege)
notes.original: l. cũ lege D. de teſta.

notes.citation: Baldus (Balde) on the Libri feudorum, De pace Constantiae (the Peace of Constance, appended to the feudal law), c. 1, § Vasall[us] (locus not verified)
notes.original: Balde au c. j. P. vaſſal. de pact. conſtant aux feudes.
notes.gloss: The print's de pact. conſtant is de pace Constantiae.

notes.original: Ariſtote au iij. liure des Ethiques.
notes.gloss: Death is the most terrible of all things, for it is the end.
The paradoxes on the wise man's indifference to death and the wicked man's fears; the passage not located.

notes.citation: Code 6.23.21, § At cum humana, cited above at {b}
notes.original: P. ad cũ humana, deſſus allegué.

blocks.html: Who is there, or how few are there, from whom, when death draws near, the timid blood does not flee back, and who does not grow pale with fear <sup class="mk" data-key="o" data-page="p144">o</sup>?

notes.citation: Cicero, De finibus, book 5 (5.31), quoting an old tragic poet
notes.gloss: Quis est, aut quotusquisque, cui mors cum adpropinquet, / non refugiat timido sanguen atque exalbescat metu? The print has cùm non appropinquet, Non refugiat, a non displaced into the first line; translated from Cicero's text.

blocks.html: And in some other place: Who is there (he says) who, being on the point of dying, has his Spirit tranquil and at rest <sup class="mk" data-key="p" data-page="p144">p</sup>?

notes.gloss: Cato on the fear of death in the old and the young; the sentence as Coras gives it is a paraphrase, the passage not located.
